analyst.summary: REC is a government-backed power and infrastructure lender with genuinely clean asset quality today (bad loans near zero) and a fast-growing renewable-energy book, and it pays a high dividend (over 5% yield) at a low earnings multiple. But look past the FY26 'highest-ever profit' headline and two things stand out: actual loan-book growth was only about 3% (well below the 11-12% management had targeted) because a wave of borrowers prepaid and refinanced elsewhere, and a large chunk of the recent profit improvement came from one-off recoveries on old stressed power loans - a tailwind that visibly faded in the March-2026 quarter, when profit fell 21% year-on-year. On top of that, REC is set to merge into its parent, Power Finance Corporation, some time around April 2027, on terms (88 PFC shares for every 100 REC shares) that look roughly fair but are not locked in and remove REC as an independent, dividend-paying, renewables-tilted investment on its own terms. We rate this a Hold: the balance sheet and yield support the stock, but the growth-quality question and the pending merger overhang keep us from being more constructive.
